who: Kirsten Fermaglich, historian of American Jewish history at Michigan State since 2001; PhD New York University 2001.

evidence.says: Her faculty biography states that she has taught history and Jewish Studies at Michigan State since 2001.
The university history center's guest biography gives her PhD as New York University, 2001, followed by employment at Michigan State.
The authority connects Kirsten Lise Fermaglich with Kirsten Fermaglich, Michigan State history and Jewish Studies faculty member and author of A Rosenberg by Any Other Name.
Crossref's metadata for her article on name changing identifies Kirsten Fermaglich, Michigan State's Department of History, with ORCID 0000-0001-6074-9708.

notes: Institution, period and doctorate match. The ORCID candidate p-6747 also identifies this scholar; p-143735 is selected as the authority-backed match.

who: Raphael Brewster Folsom, historian at the University of Oklahoma; PhD Yale 2007.

evidence.says: The 2009–11 university catalog lists Raphael Folsom as an assistant professor of history appointed in 2007, with a Yale PhD in 2007.
The history faculty list gives Raphael B. Folsom, joining in 2007 and associate professor from 2017, with a Yale PhD in 2007.
The authority for Raphael Brewster Folsom cites The Yaquis and the Empire (2014), identifying him as assistant professor of history at the University of Oklahoma.

notes: The authority's full name, Oklahoma appointment and Yale doctorate agree with the supervisor record.

who: Frank W. Fox, professor of American history at Brigham Young University during the listed student years.

evidence.says: BYU's 1998 article lists Frank W. Fox as professor of history from 1971 to the article's present.
The university archive describes a 1988 oral history with Frank W. Fox about his employment in BYU's History Department and his historical books.
The authority identifies Frank W. Fox with BYU on America's Founding Heritage (2004) and records his American history professorship there from 1971 to 2006.

notes: The full-name authority and university records place him at BYU across both student years, 1980 and 1991. The Stanford doctorate was not independently verified in this check.

who: Matthew J. (Matt) Garcia, historian at Arizona State 2011–17 and subsequently Dartmouth; PhD Claremont Graduate School 1997.

evidence.says: Dartmouth identifies Matthew J. Garcia as a historian previously employed by Arizona State and Oregon, with a PhD from Claremont Graduate School.
Matt Garcia's CV gives a 1997 US history PhD from Claremont, ASU appointments in 2011–17, and supervised theses by Aaron Bae (2017) and Rebecca Baird (2016).
The authority links Matt García and Matthew John Garcia, author of A World of Its Own and From the Jaws of Victory, and records his Oregon appointment.

notes: The CV directly identifies both listed students and matches the doctorate. It dates Bae's thesis to 2017 rather than the supplied 2016.

who: Philip Girard, legal historian formerly at Dalhousie and at York's Osgoode Hall from 2013; PhD history, Dalhousie 1998 according to his CV.

evidence.says: His profile records a Dalhousie PhD, prior employment as professor of law, history and Canadian studies at Dalhousie, and appointment at Osgoode in July 2013.
His CV gives a Dalhousie history PhD in 1998 and explicitly lists supervision of R. Blake Brown's dissertation on jury reforms, awarded the Dalhousie PhD in October 2005.
The authority identifies Philip Girard as Dalhousie's professor of law, history and Canadian studies and subsequently an Osgoode professor from 2013.
The alternative authority is for Philippe R. Girard, author of Clinton in Haiti (2004).

notes: Direct supervision of Brown confirms p-117222. The CV's doctorate year is 1998, versus 1999 in the supplied AHA record. The alternative p-101796 is the separate author Philippe R. Girard.

who: Eric L. Goldstein, historian of American Jewish history at Emory; PhD Michigan 2000.

who: Marion W. Gray, historian of Germany and gender at Western Michigan from 2001; PhD Wisconsin–Madison 1971.

The authority identifies Marion W. Gray as author of Prussia in Transition (1986) and an associate professor of history at Kansas State.

who: Lillian Guerra, professor of Cuban and Caribbean history at the University of Florida; PhD Wisconsin–Madison 2000.

evidence.says: Florida identifies Lillian Guerra as professor of Cuban and Caribbean history and author of The Myth of José Martí, Visions of Power in Cuba, and Patriots and Traitors in Revolutionary Cuba.
The 2005 profile gives her PhD as Wisconsin–Madison, 2000, and identifies her field as Latin American and Caribbean history.
A 2012 university lecture announcement identifies her as associate professor of Cuban and Caribbean history at Florida with a Wisconsin–Madison doctorate in modern Latin American history.
The authority identifies the author of Patriots and Traitors in Revolutionary Cuba as Lillian Guerra, professor of Cuban and Caribbean history at the University of Florida.

notes: The authority and university records identify the same Florida historian; the doctorate and field also match.
